issues.quote: He sent me downstairs. The regulator showed twenty past ten. It was running then, and he was well.
issues.fact: L3: He sent me downstairs when the regulator showed twenty past ten.
issues.misreading: The transcript gives the 10:20 reading as a separate sentence, not tied to the moment she was sent down. A solver could take 10:20 as a later check of the regulator rather than the departure time, so the time she left the atelier is left open.

issues.quote: Monsieur Félix would not let anyone touch his late father's silver watch, and he would not let the master touch it either.
issues.fact: L1: Monsieur Félix's watch was twenty minutes behind. The sheet says nothing about a silver watch or any other watch belonging to him.
issues.misreading: This adds a second Félix watch. A solver could wonder whether the watch he showed at nine was the silver one or a different one, which puts doubt on whether the twenty-minute reading belongs to the watch he actually carries.

issues.quote: He taught me to count the beats in my head so I would not need to look at a watch.
issues.fact: L3, L5, L6: the sheet gives the times as readings from the regulator and the kitchen clock, not as counted intervals.
issues.misreading: This suggests her sense of time is counted rather than read, which could make a solver doubt the exactness of the readings she gives, or treat the elapsed times she reports as estimates.
